blocks.p: Two mods that are turned on can carry the same code file. Only one copy is run: as a rule, the copy from the mod that loads later. The *Choose files* window lets you pick whose copy the game runs instead, file by file. Picks are for single player only.
To open the window, click *Choose file by file...* under the conflict in the *Conflicts* tab of the *Mods* window.

The list at the left of the window holds every file both mods have, its folder under its name. At the right of each row is the mod whose copy runs; a small square marks a file you have picked. The line over the list gives how many files are shared and how many are picked.

list: Click a file in the list.
Click the mod whose copy is to run.
Repeat for each file to be picked.

caption: Figure 52-1
The shared files, and the band at the window's foot.

marks.text: Every file both mods have, with the mod whose copy runs on each row.
The band sums up the picks. Use these picks puts them in a helper mod, ZeD picks, which loads last.

sticky.text: Two mods, the same file: pick whose copy runs.

blocks.p: Click a file in the list to compare its two copies. The pane at the right of the window names the file and its folder, and gives each mod's copy as a choice, with its length in lines. Under the choices the two copies are set side by side, and the lines that differ are marked. To choose whose copy the game runs, click that mod's name.

caption: Figure 52-2
The two copies of one file.

blocks.p: *Use these picks* puts the picked copies in a helper mod, ZeD picks, which loads last. A reload puts them in place; the game need not be restarted. The picks stay listed in the mod's *Conflicts* tab, with *Change picks...* to open the window again and *Undo picks* to put everything back. Any error shows in *Messages*.

caption: Figure 52-3
The Conflicts tab after the picks.

blocks.p: Mixing copies can break a mod.
